title: Pseudo-coherence is equivalent to m-pseudo-coherence for every m
statement: Let $R$ be a ring and let $D(R)$ be the derived category [def-weil-abstract-derived-category] of the abelian category of $R$-modules. For an integer $m$, call an object $C$ of $D(R)$ $m$-pseudo-coherent if there are a bounded complex $E^\bullet$ of finite free $R$-modules and a morphism $E^\bullet\to C$ in $D(R)$ inducing isomorphisms $H^i(E^\bullet)\to H^i(C)$ for $i>m$ and a surjection $H^m(E^\bullet)\to H^m(C)$. Call $C$ pseudo-coherent if it is quasi-isomorphic to a bounded-above complex of finite free $R$-modules. Let $C$ be a cochain complex of $R$-modules, viewed as an object of $D(R)$. Then $C$ is pseudo-coherent if and only if $C$ is $m$-pseudo-coherent for every integer $m$.

source.place: More on Algebra, Lemma 15.66.5 (Tag 064U), equivalence of pseudo-coherence and m-pseudo-coherence for every m

proof.text: Suppose C is pseudo-coherent, with a quasi-isomorphism from a bounded-above complex P of finite free R-modules. For any integer m, the stupid truncation of P in degrees at least m is bounded and finite free; its map to P, followed by the quasi-isomorphism to C, is an isomorphism on cohomology in degrees greater than m and a surjection in degree m. Thus C is m-pseudo-coherent.

proof.text: Conversely assume C is m-pseudo-coherent for every m. The witness for m=0 gives an upper bound b with H^i(C)=0 for i>b. Construct, by descending induction from degree b, a bounded-above complex F of finite free modules and a map F to C which is an isomorphism on H^i for i>n and surjective on H^n at stage n. If the stage-n map has cone M, the long exact sequence gives H^i(M)=0 for i>=n. The stage-n complex F (zero below degree n) is a bounded complex of finite free modules, so the identity shows it is k-pseudo-coherent for every k, in particular n-pseudo-coherent; C is (n-1)-pseudo-coherent by hypothesis. The first clause of [lem-pc-ring-pseudo-coherent-distinguished-triangle] with m=n-1, applied to the triangle F to C to M to F[1], makes M (n-1)-pseudo-coherent. Applying [lem-sc-finite-cohomology] with m=n-1 to M (which has H^i(M)=0 for i>n-1) therefore makes H^{n-1}(M) finite. Choose a finite free module mapping onto this group and lift generators to cycles (f_j,c_j) of the cone, with f_j in Ker(d^n_F) and c_j in C^{n-1} compatible with the differential; sending the j-th basis vector to f_j in F^n and to c_j in C^{n-1} is a chain map; adjoining it in degree n-1 extends F so that the map is an isomorphism in degree n and surjective in degree n-1. Repeating downward constructs F bounded above with a quasi-isomorphism F to C, so C is pseudo-coherent.
